assessment: The incumbent combines permanent identity, coarse cabinet guidance and retrospective return recording. It achieved 22/30 requests within two minutes (73.3%); only two of four closing-to-morning comparisons differed by at most one. Unfamiliar headings and concealed numbers plausibly impede navigation or identification, while frequent room transfers plausibly weaken location knowledge; neither causal account is established. The limiting observation is that all 48 items were present last Friday and no missing equipment was recorded: failed requests need not imply inventory loss or insufficient total stock. Conversely, presence does not establish availability during requests. Morning comparisons also do not isolate closing-count accuracy without knowing intervening movements. The 14-minute count establishes effort, not whether workshops were interrupted.

openings.claim: Are delayed requests chiefly navigation failures, failures to locate equipment already at tables, or genuine simultaneous unavailability?
openings.delta: Separates explanations that call for different changes; clearer cabinet headings alone may leave the dominant delay untouched.
openings.prediction: A navigation explanation predicts idle matching items during delays and substantial time at cabinets or interpreting headings. A room-location explanation predicts idle matching items elsewhere. A capacity explanation predicts all matching items in use.
openings.probe: During the next session, use a brief paper tally of request duration, search location, heading confusion and visibly idle matching equipment. Observe without redirecting participants or interrupting activities; mark availability unknown whenever both rooms cannot be checked. Compare patterns among timely, delayed and abandoned requests before choosing an intervention.
assumptions: A volunteer can observe a useful subset without neglecting workshop duties.
Observation uses existing stationery and fits within the two-hour initial preparation allowance; no personal information is collected.

openings.claim: Some closing-to-morning differences may reflect intervening location changes or inconsistent count coverage rather than erroneous return recording.
openings.delta: Tests whether the current comparison measures the intended inventory accuracy.
openings.prediction: Closing counts that agree with a contemporaneous physical check but disagree with morning counts support a timing or coverage explanation. Immediate disagreement supports a closing enumeration or recording problem.
openings.probe: At normal workshop close, compare the recorded count with a physical checklist using existing asset numbers across both rooms, tables and cabinets. Note locations and any movements during checking; repeat the same coverage next morning. Treat untracked movements or a noncontemporaneous check as unresolved evidence.
assumptions: Verification can occur after scheduled activities without interrupting workshops.
Printing and preparation fit within 60 currency units and two initial steward hours, jointly with Z1; ongoing verification time must be recorded.
